title: Edge traffic consolidation fallback cheat sheet
content:
Purpose:
This is an on-call cheat sheet and post-incident sketch for a mitigation pattern we trialed in Q1: consolidating user traffic into a reduced subset of regions (traffic condensation) as a short-lived fallback to bound KV-cache divergence and reduce cross-region network surface during partial-region degradation.

Scope and when to use it:
- Trigger when more than one edge region shows elevated 5xx or TCP retransmit rates and latency SLOs are breached, but global control plane remains healthy.
- Useful if (a) kvcache warmup across regions is slow and causes inconsistent prefixes, or (b) egress asymmetry is amplifying cascading retries and client-side failover oscillation.
- Not intended as a full region evacuation; prefer for 15–90 minute containment windows.

Observed benefits in experiment run on 2025-02-26:
- Median p95 generation latency dropped 18% after consolidating to 3 regions.
- Cross-region KV-miss rate on critical prefix decreased from 12% to 3% within 200s.
- Overall error budget burn slowed; however, tail latency improved more slowly for long sequences.

Quick decision checklist (operator):
1) Confirm degradation pattern: consult edge-latency, edge-5xx, and cross-region-retry dashboards.
2) Verify control plane and model-serving control pods are green (no downstream rollout interfering).
3) Check KV-cache priming status for hotspots (kvcache-misses by prefix).
4) Confirm customer-impacting routes list (console->routes->top-traffic).
5) Decide consolidation target
